messages:
incident-bot: [PAGER] P0 - serving-cluster-prod-us-east high error rate (CUDA OOMs + container restarts). Paging @oncall-sre @oncall-ml @alex

pagerduty: Incident created: INC-2026-1975 - 1975004321

alex: seeing a spike in 5xxs and pods are in CrashLoopBackOff on gpu-nodepool-2. autoscaler kept adding nodes then they immediately flapped.

maria: logs show repeated 'CUDA out of memory' from runtime v2.3.1, tied to long seq requests. traceback attached.

chen: can someone check recent rollout? any model changes or quantization toggles?

kyra: no model rollout in the last 2 hours. infra autoscaler had a policy change at 1975001200 to more aggressive scale-up. might be oscillation.

alex: stack dump snippet:

```
2026-03-15T14:12:09Z runtime ERROR: cudaMalloc failed: out of memory
stack: runtime/allocator.c:112
```

maria: Also seeing KV cache memory growth on long-context requests. Batching + long-seq => peak memory > device.

oncall-ml: marking impacted customers: two enterprise tenants reporting latency and 502s. dialing AE.

oncall-sre: I'm taking lead for infra actions. first mitigations: 1) pause autoscaler 2) cordon problematic nodes 3) reduce max replicas on the deployment to prevent immediate scale up.

alex: I'm on pod logs and preparing a quick rollback to runtime v2.3.0 (last stable). prepping helm rollback cmd.

chen: Suggest temp change to model concurrency config: set --max-seq to 1024 for prod route to cap memory. Can we patch via configmap?

kyra: patch ready. applying configmap patch now. command:

```
kubectl -n prod patch configmap runtime-config -p '{"data":{"max_seq":"1024"}}'
```

infra-ops-bot: autoscaler: scaled from 12 -> 26 -> 9 nodes in last 10m. damping windows insufficient. (metric: gpu_utilization, threshold: 0.65)

oncall-sre: disabling cluster-autoscaler for the pool (will hold capacity steady). command run.

pagerduty: @oncall-sre acknowledged at 1975004365

oncall-sre: cordoned nodes: gpu-node-17, gpu-node-19, gpu-node-22 (evicting pods gracefully).

maria: rollback to runtime v2.3.0 initiated for deployment serving-runtime-prod, rolling restart started.

alex: also temporarily reducing replica count to 6 to limit simultaneous warmups.

chen: traffic routing note: enabling fallback to cpu-backed small-llm model for low-latency async requests to reduce GPU pressure.

kyra: customer-facing: created a status page incident and posted initial note 'We are investigating increased errors in model inference; mitigation in progress.'

oncall-ml: AE update sent to impacted accounts with ETA ~30m, asked for logs and sample requests.

maria: after rollback, crashloops reduced but not fully resolved. still seeing OOM on a subset of requests where seq > 1500.

alex: applying runtime guard to reject > 1200 token seq at router level for now. patching gateway config.

```
PATCH /gateway/config
{"body_size_limit":1200}
```

pagerduty: update 1975004700 - oncall-sre changed incident state -> mitigation in progress

infra-ops-bot: node reboots observed on gpu-node-19 due to kubelet OOM kill during eviction process — investigating kubelet memory usage.

kyra: ops note: we'll keep autoscaler disabled for 1h and monitor metrics. any objection?

oncall-ml: agree. need to watch latency and cost impact of offloading to CPU fallback.

chen: created a short-lived helm override to set batching window to 5ms to avoid large batch memory spikes.

maria: after batching tweak + rollback + max_seq cap, error rate dropped from 18% -> 2.2% over 12 minutes. some 502s persist for long-running requests that bypass routing limits.

oncall-sre: okay prepping for handoff in 30m. documenting runbook steps taken and remaining actions: 1) re-enable autoscaler with higher damping 2) bump node kubelet memory limits 3) upstream patch for runtime v2.3.2 to avoid KV cache leak 4) evaluate long-seq gating per-customer

alex: saving logs and core dumps to /mnt/incident/1975004321/ for postmortem.

oncall-ml: AE on call has been notified for follow up.

pagerduty: handoff scheduled: @oncall-sre -> @kyra at 1975005700.

kyra: I've taken over. monitoring dashboard shows GPU mem tail still with occasional spikes when a customer runs long-history prompts. will coordinate with solutions to apply per-tenant rate limits.

maria: creating postmortem ticket INC-2026-1975-PM and attaching timeline + artifacts.

chen: followups: test autoscaler damping patch in staging, add model-level sequence caps, instrument per-token memory accounting.

kyra: thanks team. keeping status page updated every 15m until fully resolved. :thumbsup:
